author: Latham, 1801
status: 나그네새 수천 마리 · 여름철새 수십 마리
habitat: 산지 숲과 능선·계곡 위의 하늘, 바닷가와 섬

months.note: 봄에는 5월, 가을에는 9~10월에 지나가는 무리가 가장 많고, 4월 하순에 일찍 오는 개체도 있다.

summary: 봄·가을 이동기에 수천 마리가 지나가는 나그네새이고, 수십 마리는 여름에 남아 높은 산의 숲에서 번식하는 것으로 추정된다. 시베리아 중·동부에서 사할린, 몽골 북부, 중국 동북부, 한반도, 일본에 걸쳐 번식하고, 겨울에는 뉴기니 남부와 오스트레일리아 동부로 간다. 오래된 큰 나무의 구멍이나 바위 절벽 틈에 둥지를 틀고, 매우 빠르게 날며 딱정벌레·벌·파리·나방 같은 날벌레를 잡아먹는다.

art.subject: White-throated Needletail (Hirundapus caudacutus), adult as seen over Korea on migration in May and September: forehead and lores whitish; crown, face, nape, wings and tail blackish-brown with a faint green gloss; throat clean white, sharply defined; back with a large pale grey-brown, silvery saddle; breast and belly dark brown; a sharply defined white horseshoe running from the rear flanks around the undertail coverts; inner webs of the tertials white, showing as a small white patch near the body on the upperwing; short, square black tail with bare spine-like shaft tips. Tiny black bill; dark eye.
art.pose: gliding fast and low over a forested ridge, seen squarely from below: both long, narrow, scythe-shaped wings spread out to the sides and swept back in a crescent from the wrist, white throat, dark brown body, sharply defined white horseshoe around the undertail, short square tail with needle tips, and the small dark feet just visible tucked against the belly
art.scene: Korean mountain ridge with mixed forest during spring migration in May, wide sky with scattered clouds; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, in flight seen squarely from below: long, narrow, scythe-shaped wings spread out from the shoulders and swept back from the wrist, whitish forehead, sharply defined white throat, dark brown body, white horseshoe from the rear flanks around the undertail coverts, short square tail with needle tips, small dark feet tucked against the belly

adult, in flight seen squarely from above: whitish forehead, blackish-brown crown and nape, large pale silvery grey-brown saddle on the back, long scythe-shaped dark wings with a faint green gloss swept back from the wrist, small white tertial patch near the body, dark rump, short square black tail with needle tips
art.build: Very large, heavy, powerful swift, noticeably bigger and bulkier than the Pacific Swift, with a thick, cigar-shaped body, long scythe-shaped pointed wings and a short, square tail tipped with protruding needle-like shafts. Flies extremely fast, sweeping and gliding on stiff wings, often low over ridges and water. Never perches on branches; in flight the small dark feet are tucked against the belly, just visible from below.
avoid: Do not paint a forked tail or a white rump band — those mark Pacific Swift; this species has a short square tail and a dark rump.
Do not show it perched on a branch or wire, or with long tail streamers like a swallow.
Do not omit the white throat and the white horseshoe around the undertail.
Do not make the wings broad or rounded; they are long, narrow and scythe-shaped.
Do not paint the bird banking with one wing raised and the other lowered; show both wings spread symmetrically.
